text:
sam: Quick check — how should our SDK map Redwood API error shapes -> language exceptions? Two angle: normal request errors (401/403/429/5xx) and streaming failures (mid-stream 502 / connection reset). Also want a recommended pattern for logging request_id so support can trace failures.

lina: For mapping: keep it simple and consistent across SDKs. Suggested mapping: 401/403 -> AuthError, 404 -> NotFoundError, 429 -> RateLimitError (include retry-after if present), other 4xx -> BadRequestError, 5xx -> ServerError. Stream failures get StreamError with context.

mike: +1. Important: attach the request_id from the HTTP header (x-request-id) to the exception object so callers can log it or surface it. Example Python pattern: 
```py
# exceptions.py
class APIError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, status=None, request_id=None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.request_id = request_id

class RateLimitError(APIError): pass
class AuthError(APIError): pass
class StreamError(APIError): pass
```
When raising, pass request_id: raise RateLimitError(msg, status=429, request_id=req_id)

jen: For streaming specifically, prefer an error that includes last_event_id or last_consumed_offset so caller can attempt resume if supported. If it's a terminal 5xx, we should surface a StreamError that includes request_id and whether the SDK attempted any internal retries.

lina: Also add structured logging convention in SDK: always log at debug level with the request id key. e.g. in Python: logger.debug("req failed", extra={"request_id": req_id, "status": status}) or simple formatted: logger.debug(f"[request_id={req_id}] status={status} msg={msg}")

mike: Node example for mapping + retry hint: 
```js
// on response
const reqId = res.headers['x-request-id'];
if (res.status === 429) throw new RateLimitError('rate limited', { status: 429, requestId: reqId, retryAfter: res.headers['retry-after'] });
```
This keeps runtime info in the error object.

sam: How about streaming reconnect/backoff behavior? If chunk fails mid-stream with a connection reset, should SDK auto-retry or bubble up?

jen: For user-facing SDKs, try 1 internal reconnect for transient network blips (with small backoff) and if still failing, raise StreamError with request_id and a resume_token if available. Make attempts configurable via client options. Default: retries=1, backoff=200ms.

lina: Also document deterministic ids: if server provides "x-request-id" use that; if not, SDK should generate a UUID and include it in outgoing header "x-client-request-id" and log it. That way support traces can correlate client+server.

eng-platform-bot: NOTE: We'll add a test matrix for error shapes across SDKs next sprint. @lina @mike please add unit tests to validate exception types + request_id propagation.

mike: Will add tests. Quick unit example (pytest): 
```py
def test_rate_limit_exc_includes_request_id(client, responses):
    responses.add(429, headers={"x-request-id": "rid-123"})
    with pytest.raises(RateLimitError) as e:
        client.call(...)
    assert e.value.request_id == "rid-123"
```

sam: Perfect. Can we also agree on log message style so SRE can grep? Proposed: "[rid=<id>] <component> <action> status=<code> msg=<short>". If everyone ok I'll file a tiny doc in devex docs and link examples.

lina: ok by me.

jen: ok. Filing followups: 1) update SDK exception reference 2) add streaming resume example 3) add test coverage. @mike can you PR the python snippets?

mike: On it, targetting a small PR with tests tomorrow. :thumbsup:
